title: A Yearbook for the Scholarship
premise: In the fading mill town of Harrow Bend, Sable Underhill has perfected invisibility — until her best friend, scholarship-bound Theo Vance, vanishes overnight, leaving behind his car keys and a half-finished application essay naming a teacher he trusted. Following the trail, Sable uncovers a scheme to funnel scholarship funds to the school board chairman's nephew, and evidence that Theo found out. As the town closes ranks and the sheriff — the chairman's brother-in-law — calls Theo a runaway, Sable and a wary new ally, Theo's ex-girlfriend Priya, build a case outside the law: a yearbook of testimonies from every kid the system failed. In the climax, Sable trades her own anonymity to broadcast the truth at the scholarship assembly, and Theo — held at a 'troubled teen' facility across state lines to silence him — is brought home. Sable learns that justice sometimes requires becoming visible, and that love, for Theo and for herself, was never a detour from duty but the duty itself.
about_author: I. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent a decade watching brilliant students slip through administrative cracks. They write from a farmhouse that is, by their own admission, far too full of old yearbooks.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Head Down
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Establishes Harrow Bend's claustrophobia and Sable's careful choreography of invisibility — the only out kid in nine hundred people, surviving by routine. Her one exception is Theo, her best friend since third grade, who jokes about escaping on his scholarship. Beat: the ache of a life lived in miniature.

chapters.title: The Empty Passenger Seat
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Theo doesn't show for their morning carpool. By third period his desk is empty; by nightfall his mother is on the porch, and his car sits at the overlook with the keys still in the ignition. The sheriff calls it a runaway. Sable knows Theo would never leave without saying goodbye. Beat: dread arriving in slow motion.

chapters.title: Keys and Half-Truths
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Searching Theo's locker before it's cleared, Sable finds his draft scholarship essay — naming a beloved teacher, Mr. Aldous, as his mentor — and a note in the margin: 'ask about the second account.' Priya, Theo's ex, confronts Sable, convinced Sable knows more. Beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Priya at the Diner Counter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Priya's first. Priya reveals Theo had been pulling records for weeks — printouts, a flash drive, a fear he wouldn't explain. The two girls, awkward ex-rivals, form a reluctant alliance. Beat: two lonely people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Chairman's Nephew
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The scholarship that should have been Theo's — and before him, three other kids' — went to board chairman Dale Merrick's nephew, whose grades don't qualify. Sable maps four missing students across six years, all 'runaways.' Beat: the pattern clicking into place, cold and enormous.

chapters.title: What the Yearbooks Remember
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. In the library archive, Priya notices each vanished kid appears in fewer and fewer photos, erased from memory as surely as from enrollment. She proposes the idea that becomes their weapon: a people's yearbook, testimonies of everyone the town failed. Beat: purpose igniting.

chapters.title: Mr. Aldous, After Hours
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confronts Aldous, who is terrified, complicit-adjacent, and pitiful: he signed paperwork he didn't read to keep his job. He gives them one thread — the name of the 'placement consultant' Merrick uses. Beat: disillusionment; heroes have rent to pay.

chapters.title: The Facility Called Second Chance
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Researching the consultant leads to Second Chance Academy, a for-profit behavioral facility two states away that receives county payments per 'placement.' A former resident's blog post describes kids who arrived in the night. Beat: horror reframing 'runaway' as a euphemism.

chapters.title: Sheriff Dane Knows Your Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The sheriff summons Sable, warns her off 'conspiracy nonsense,' and lets slip that he knows about the flash drive. Sable realizes she's being watched — and that Theo's disappearance is being managed, not investigated. Beat: fear with a badge.

chapters.title: The First Testimony
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The girls interview Dana Whitfield, a vanished student now working nights at a truck stop, who confirms she was sent to Second Chance after asking about the scholarship fund. She agrees to record her story. The yearbook begins. Beat: courage is contagious.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Under Surveillance
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Homecoming week; the town performs normalcy while Sable collects testimonies in a notebook disguised as a yearbook signing book. Someone goes through her locker; her tires are slashed. Theo's mother, breaking, begs Sable to stop. Beat: the cost of truth made personal.

chapters.title: What I Never Told Him
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, intimate and confessional. A quiet chapter of flashback: the summer night Sable came out to Theo, his fierce loyalty, and the love she never named because naming it would change everything. Beat: love against duty — her silence as both protection and cowardice.

chapters.title: The Flash Drive
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Following Theo's habits, Priya deduces he hid the flash drive inside the trophy case — inside the yearbook trophy itself. Inside: transfer authorizations with Sheriff Dane's signature and a ledger of payments from Second Chance. Beat: the smoking gun, and the terror of holding it.

chapters.title: Copy, Hide, Copy Again
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A tense logistics chapter: duplicating the evidence, mailing a copy to a state journalist, hiding the original. Aldous, guilt-ridden, finally agrees to testify — then doesn't show the next day and won't answer his phone. Beat: allies are fragile.

chapters.title: They Found the Notebook
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Sable's house is searched 'for missing persons leads'; the testimony notebook is seized as evidence. Sheriff Dane warns Sable that obstruction carries juvenile charges. Priya's copy survives. Beat: rock bottom — the law itself as the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Assembly Gambit
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The scholarship assembly will honor Merrick's nephew with the whole town present, plus a visiting education reporter. Sable and Priya plan to hijack it: swap the presentation slideshow with their evidence. Sable volunteers to be the one on stage. Beat: decision crystallizing — visibility chosen.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Minutes
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The assembly, in near-real-time. The swap half-works; the slideshow plays testimonies over the auditorium speakers as Merrick blusters and Dane moves to cut the power. Sable takes the microphone and reads the names of the vanished. Beat: climax — a small voice made enormous.

chapters.title: Where They Keep the Quiet Kids
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The broadcast forces the state's hand: an investigator traces the placements, and Second Chance is raided. Theo is found — drugged into compliance, alive, three hundred miles away. Beat: catharsis and fury in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Long Drive Home
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sable and Priya drive through the night to bring Theo back. On the highway, Sable finally says the thing she never told him. Theo, hollowed but himself, says he knew. Beat: love named at last, against every rule of timing.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Hearings begin; Dane and Merrick fall, Aldous testifies through tears. The town splits between relief and resentment — some thank the girls, some spit. Beat: justice outside the law turns out to be slow once the law arrives.

chapters.title: The Yearbook, Printed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The kids of Harrow Bend publish the people's yearbook themselves — testimonies, photos, the names of the vanished restored to every page. Sable's own entry, written in her hand, is the truest thing she's ever signed. Beat: memory as monument.

chapters.title: Locker Open
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Graduation-adjacent epilogue: Theo, scholarship reinstated under his own name; Priya and Sable, together now; Sable walking the halls head up, locker decorated, visible. The last line mirrors the first chapter — same town, same kid, no longer hiding. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
